issues.reason: A dependent existential keeps its typing inside the conclusion (the every-student-read-some-book rule emits (Member (sk_book $x) book) there), and only a wide-scope shared existential earns a top-level constant plus typing (the some-critic-reviewed-every-film pattern) — so with the universal taking wide scope here, (Member sk_station_1 station) and (Near sk_station_1 sunken_cove) assert a station's existence and position unconditionally when the sentence posits it only under the conditional.

The scope tiebreak is "genuine ambiguity -> first quantifier takes wide scope" and only "the same"/"a certain" forces the shared reading; "whenever" is the first quantifier and no such cue is present, so the requester is a dependent existential requiring (sk_station $d), and the shared constant asserts that one and the same station answers every draining.

The half that stands is that the event-locative attachment (Location $d sunken_cove) is the favored reading of "drains a lantern at the Sunken Cove" and the parse does not carry it; the half that overstates is calling the emitted atom wrong — "at" is containment, so (LocatedIn $l sunken_cove) is true and well-typed under the equally coherent nominal attachment, making this a reading choice rather than a false or ill-typed atom.

new_gaps: the whenever / every-time section works only definite consequent participants ("the dog"), so an indefinite introduced in a whenever-consequent has no worked pattern saying whether it is a dependent Skolem function of the trigger occurrence or a shared constant — the scope tiebreak is stated only for "a clause with two quantifiers over a relation"

PP attachment inside a whenever-trigger clause has no legislated preference: nothing says when a locative on the trigger event vs. on its object is a genuine tie that should fire the Interpretation dual-reading rather than a world-knowledge lean to be resolved silently
defect_summary: For issues 0 and 1 the compliant form mints the requester as a dependent existential inside the conclusion — (Member (sk_station $d) station), (Near (sk_station $d) sunken_cove), (Agent (sk_request $d) (sk_station $d)) — with no top-level station atoms; the Sunken Cove Name + cove type, the feather_ration genus, and the top-level Council typing (a definite, which projects) all stay as they are, and the favored attachment for issue 2 would put (Location $d sunken_cove) on the draining event.
notes: The name handling is correct on both counts (the capitalized run exceeds the bare class word, so Name + cove type and no modifier genus; "the Council" stays a common noun with no Name), as are Source for "from the Council", the entity-attached Near, Patient on the drained lantern, and the absent QuantifierPhrase companion.
